ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, and Steam/PlayStation payout counterparties against: (i) United Nations Consolidated Security Council Sanctions List; (ii) Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List under SEMA and related federal regulations; (iii) OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists (mandatory for USD clearing of Steam/PlayStation payouts); (iv) FINTRAC PCMLTFA enhanced due diligence standards for politically exposed persons (PEPs) and foreign PEPs; and (v) domestic and international adverse-media and high-risk-jurisdiction indicators, with transaction monitoring. Compliance program formation and MSB registration thresholds under the PCMLTFA must be assessed if aggregated payment settlement volumes exceed FINTRAC screening thresholds.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ontario Business Registry (ServiceOntario) - online portal at ontario.ca/page/ontario-business-registry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A proposed name must be filed in Latin-script characters exactly as presented in the pre-filing NUANS name search report; French, English, and bilingual names are permitted; non-Latin or transliterated commercial names must be rendered in Romanized form in the NUANS report and Articles of Incorporation; the name must satisfy OBCA distinctiveness and non-confusion requirements against existing corporate names, business names, and registered trademarks under O. Reg 62, R.R.O. 1990.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days of a name-rejection notice, the applicant may file a written notice of objection with the Director of Corporate Services through the Ontario Business Registry, attaching supporting trademark registrations or evidence of prior use for distinctiveness reassessment; if the Director sustains the refusal, the applicant may seek judicial review before the Ontario Divisional Court under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, RSO 1990, c J.1. Alternatively, the applicant may immediately file a fresh NUANS search for a revised name, thereby opening a new 90-day reservation window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for Ontario digital-publishing corporations subject to strict limits: the registered office must be a real, staffed physical street address within Ontario where statutory corporate records (articles, by-laws, directors' register, ISC/UBO register, and minutes) are retained and inspectable during normal business hours; a P.O. Box or unstaffed mail drop is non-compliant; a licensed virtual-office package providing reception, mail handling, and meeting-room access satisfies OBCA registered-office requirements for this low-risk software-publishing industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 3-5% annual probability absent a triggering complaint or adverse AML/sanctions flag; probability rises to approximately 15% if the registered-office address is flagged as a non-compliant virtual-office cluster or if statutory records are absent during a ServiceOntario corporate-compliance inspection).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ontario Business Corporations Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. B.16 (OBCA), ss. 4 (incorporation), 5 (articles of incorporation), 23 (share consideration), 97 (registered office), 118 (resident Canadian directors), 115-121 (board of directors), 184 (corporate records); Ontario Business Registry regulation O. Reg 262/21; federal registration under Income Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.), s. 227, and Excise Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. E-15, s. 240 (GST/HST).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ontario Business Registry (OBR), administered by the Companies and Personal Property Security Branch (CIPPSB) of the Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery and Procurement (MPBSDP), ServiceOntario.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (OBCA Form 1) filed electronically through the Ontario Business Registry portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement for a non-offering corporation. The articles may authorize one or more classes of shares; common shares are typically issued to the incorporator for nominal consideration of CAD 1.00 in cash. At least one director, or 25% of directors where there are more than three, must be resident Canadians per OBCA s. 118.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporator's subscription for 100 Common Shares (no par value) at CAD 0.01 per share is hereby accepted and issued for CAD 1.00 in cash. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Corporation's registered office shall be maintained at [Street Address], [City], Ontario, as its statutory seat, and the directors are authorized to execute leases and file notices respecting the office. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the following officers are appointed until the first annual shareholders' meeting: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary. FURTHER RESOLVED, that management is authorized to execute all filings and contracts required to carry out these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS name search if a named corporation is desired; the report must confirm corporate name availability. File the name reservation through the Ontario Business Registry online portal, or alternatively incorporate directly with a numbered name (e.g., '12345678 Ontario Inc.') without reservation. The director(s) must confirm the proposed name contains no prohibited keywords and is sufficiently distinguishable.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search report (issued within 90 days prior to filing)
Proposed corporate name and keyword list
Name reservation application submitted via Ontario Business Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to conflict, trademark similarity, or prohibited keyword, amend the proposed name by adding a distinguishing element and resubmit with a new or updated NUANS search; alternatively, proceed with a numbered company name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Articles of Incorporation Filing and Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Registry / CIPPSB, Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery and Procurement
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the Ontario Business Registry portal and complete OBCA Form 1 online: provide the corporate name or numbered name, the municipality of the registered office in Ontario, the first director(s) (with mandatory resident Canadian representation), the authorized share structure (e.g., unlimited Common Shares and Preferred Shares), and any transfer restrictions. Submit electronically and pay the CAD 300 filing fee. Upon approval, the Registry issues the Certificate of Incorporation and assigns the Ontario corporation number.
required_dossiers: Completed OBCA Form 1 / Ontario Business Registry online application
NUANS name search report (for named companies)
Corporate name and registered office municipality in Ontario
Director consent forms (Form 2 declarations, electronically captured)
Payment of CAD 300 filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry queries the filing (e.g., deficiency in director residency or share provisions), rectify the flagged item and resubmit the corrected Form 1; the filing fee may be retained but the correction is processed on an expedited basis. If incorporation is refused on public-interest grounds, file under a differently styled name or use a numbered company designation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office Establishment and Organizational Resolutions (Minute Book)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation (recorded in Minute Book) with ServiceOntario registered office address registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Establish the registered office at a physical address within Ontario, obtain the landlord's consent or lease agreement, and file the registered office address in the corporate records. Convene the first board of directors meeting to approve the first board resolution, adopt Bylaw No. 1, authorize issuance of share certificates, appoint officers, approve the banking resolution, and set the fiscal year end. Maintain the securities register, director register, and officer register per OBCA ss. 99 and 184.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Registered office lease or landlord consent letter
Bylaw No. 1 (general operating bylaw)
First Board Resolution (minutes of the organizational meeting)
Securities register and share certificates
Minute book covers, director register, and officer register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office lease or consent is unavailable, change the registered office to an alternative Ontario address, re-execute the lease and consent, and file the updated address through the Ontario Business Registry within 15 days per OBCA s. 99.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Tax Registration (BN, GST/HST, Payroll, Ontario Corporate Tax)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration / My Business Account; Ontario Ministry of Finance via ONT-TAX-ONLINE
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for the CRA Business Number (BN) and elect the applicable program accounts: corporate income tax (RC0001), GST/HST account (mandatory once annual taxable revenue exceeds CAD 30,000 per Excise Tax Act s. 240), payroll deductions account (if employees are hired), and import/export program account (if applicable). Register the Ontario Corporation Tax account with the Ministry of Finance to receive T2 corporate tax filings and Ontario tax instalments. Complete all registrations electronically through CRA and ONT-TAX-ONLINE, describing the business activity as NAICS 511210 software publishing.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Ontario corporation number
Legal corporate name, registered office address, and director details
First fiscal year-end date and business activity description (NAICS 511210)
Directors' social insurance numbers or passport/ID for non-resident directors
Canadian bank account details for CRA direct deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA suspends or delays a program account, file a correction or reactivation through My Business Account or Form RC159; if the Ontario Ministry of Finance issues a reassessment, file a Notice of Objection within 90 days under the Income Tax Act s. 165 or the Ontario Taxation Act s. 95.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Occupancy, Fire Safety, and Workplace Safety Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal building and fire services (e.g., City of Toronto Building and Fire Prevention); Ontario Ministry of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development; Workplace Safety and Insurance Board (WSIB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the corporation leases or owns commercial office premises for publishing operations, verify that the intended use (General Office / Business Services) is a permitted use under the municipal zoning by-law and obtain an occupancy permit under the Building Code Act, 1992. Conduct an Ontario Fire Code (O. Reg 213/07) inspection, install fire safety equipment as required, and file a fire safety/evacuation plan. Register for WSIB coverage under O. Reg 175/98 Schedule 1 within 10 days of hiring employees and post the Occupational Health and Safety Act workplace poster.
required_dossiers: Commercial lease agreement or proof of occupancy rights
Zoning verification letter from municipal planning department
Fire safety plan, floor plan, and egress drawings
Municipal occupancy permit or clearance letter
WSIB registration confirmation and payroll reporting schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A fire inspection order to remedy non-compliance requires a municipal reinspection by the stated deadline; building code violations may be appealed to the municipal Property Standards Committee or the Building Code Commission; WSIB assessments and experience-rating disputes are appealable under the Workplace Safety and Insurance Act, 1997.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ontario Ministry of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development (occupational health and safety); local municipal building and fire services (physical occupancy). No industrial manufacturing or sectoral publishing license is applicable to ISIC 5820 digital software publishing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial Office Occupancy Permit and Fire Safety Clearance under the Building Code Act, 1992 and Ontario Fire Code (O. Reg 213/07); no sectoral video game publishing license is required in Ontario.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks (MECP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Class B (administrative/office use) generates no prescribed undertaking under the Environmental Assessment Act or Environmental Protection Act; no Environmental Compliance Approval (ECA) required; optional e-waste registration under O. Reg 347/90 and the Resource Recovery and Circular Economy Act, 2016 if waste electrical and electronic equipment volumes exceed prescribed thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emission sources; sanitary discharges must comply with the applicable municipal sewer use by-law (e.g., City of Toronto Sewers By-law 850-2013); hazardous waste manifests per O. Reg 347/90 for any discarded electronics; GHG reporting under O. Reg 390/18 is inapplicable below 10,000 t CO2e annually.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Ontario Fire Code (O. Reg 213/07) fire safety inspection certificate; Building Code Act, 1992 occupancy and structural load verification; Occupational Health and Safety Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. O.1 workplace hazard assessment; WSIB workplace safety and insurance registration for all employees; Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, 2005 (AODA) customer service and employment standards compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — the federal authority administering the GST/HST, Part I federal corporate income tax, and the Ontario provincial corporate income tax on behalf of the Ontario Ministry of Finance under the Federal-Provincial Tax Collection Agreement. Registration and filings are performed through CRA's My Business Account portal and GST/HST NETFILE (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html). The Ontario Ministry of Finance (https://www.ontario.ca/page/ministry-finance) retains ancillary administration of provincial levies not collected by the CRA.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the central monetary authority responsible for the Canadian dollar and exchange-rate policy. Canada maintains no statutory foreign-exchange control regime; the administrative perimeter is instead covered by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential bank supervision, the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for anti-money-laundering/anti-terrorist-financing surveillance of cross-border electronic funds transfers, and Payments Canada for the operation of the large-value clearing system (Lynx).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully and freely convertible on both current-account and capital-account transactions. The Exchange Control Act was repealed in 1951, and no licence, prior approval, repatriation quota, or conversion mandate applies to profit remittance, capital injection, or trade settlements. The only profit-repatriation hurdle is tax-based: dividends paid by CA_CORP to non-resident shareholders attract Part XIII withholding tax (statutory 25%, treaty-reduced, typically to 5–15% under Canada's income tax conventions), but the underlying foreign-currency wire is unrestricted. USD revenue received from Valve (Steam) and Sony (PlayStation Store) may be retained, converted, or remitted freely without central-bank clearance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Canada imposes no statutory surrender, conversion, or repatriation obligation on export proceeds; the historical Exchange Control Act surrender regime was abolished in 1951. CA_CORP may lawfully retain Steam and PlayStation Store USD receipts in a Canadian USD-denominated account or in any offshore account of its Treasury. The sole compliance overlay is FINTRAC's large-EFT reporting threshold of CAD $10,000 or more per cross-border transfer, which the reporting bank discharges at the point of receipt or dispatch; OSFI net-open-currency-position rules apply to the banking counterparty, not to the non-financial corporate exporter.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Operational Account (dual CAD and USD cross-border)
Operational Account and Commercial Trade Finance / LC Facility
Secondary Operational Account for Francophone and EU-facing treasury flows

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. A purely offshore electronic money institution (EMI) without Canadian registration cannot clear CAD, participate in Lynx settlement, or offer CDIC-insured deposits, and therefore is not a substitute for a tier-1 operating account. However, FINTRAC-registered Money Services Businesses with Canadian presence (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, OFX) are viably used as overlay rails for collecting USD storefront payouts from Valve and Sony and for executing low-value international disbursements to co-publishers. A Schedule III branch of a foreign bank under the Bank Act is legally permissible but commercially impracticable and capital-inefficient for a mid-market software publisher.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not statutorily mandated under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), but Canadian tier-1 banks in practice require at least one director or a designated officer with signing authority to complete an in-person interview at a Canadian branch for first-time corporate account onboarding. Remote video-identity KYC is accepted by RBC, TD, and BMO only where the director holds valid Canadian government-issued photo identification and the company maintains a registered office in Canada; any non-resident director or beneficial owner will trigger mandatory enhanced due diligence, and banks may require physical attendance of the principal UBO at the onboarding branch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity: FINTRAC and the Canada Business Corporations Act require identification and verification of every individual with significant control (shareholder or other person who exercises control, typically 25% or more of voting rights or fair-market value), and Ontario's corporate registry rules mandate corresponding reporting.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Significant Control Persons Register maintained under s. 2.1 CBCA or OBCA; Certificate of Incorporation (Federal or Ontario); Ontario Business Information Report; notarized organizational chart; individual UBO declarations with full name, date of birth, residential address, and shareholding percentage; government-issued photo ID (passport or Ontario driver's licence) for every significant-control individual.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth and source-of-funds on the initial inbound shareholder capital subscription or shareholder loan.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of bank statements for the originating shareholder/entity; executed equity subscription agreement or shareholder loan agreement; proof of business legitimacy (business plan, revenue forecast, published storefront pipeline); sworn source-of-funds declaration; and, where the funding party is a non-resident corporation, a tax-residency certificate and a Part XIII withholding-law analysis confirming that injected share capital is not taxable Canadian income.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recurring large USD credits from foreign digital-platform payers (Valve Corporation, Sony Interactive Entertainment) may be flagged as unverified third-party funding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Steamworks Distribution Agreement with Valve; PlayStation Partner digital publishing agreement with Sony; storefront revenue dashboards for the trailing three months; W-8BEN-E (Canada-US tax form) evidencing beneficial-owner status in the US; payout advice statements from each platform; and a corporate treasury resolution identifying the approved payout counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border transfer frequency and jurisdiction screening: Steam/PlayStation remittances originate from US, EU, and JP legal entities and may produce false-positive sanctions hits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed screening of all counterparties against the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, and EU Consolidated List at account opening and quarterly thereafter; commercial contract extracts proving end-customer and counterparty identity; annual certification by the compliance officer that no sanctioned person owns, controls, or brokers the platform payouts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered-office mismatch, incomplete director mandates, or insufficient signing-authority governance for treasury operations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Ontario Business Information Report reflecting the registered office; board resolution appointing two signing officers with dual-signature authority for all wires above CAD $25,000; specimen signature cards certified by the corporate secretary; and the company's banking resolution form executed in accordance with the CBCA/OBCA by-law.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital is delivered by SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's bank to the CA_CORP tier-1 operational CAD account; the payment narrative must state the company legal name, corporate registration number, and an IMF BPM6-aligned purpose descriptor such as 'equity injection — direct investment' or 'shareholder loan' to avoid mischaracterization as Canadian-source revenue. CAD settlement occurs in real time over the Payments Canada Lynx RTGS system; USD-denominated injections are cleared through the Canadian bank's US correspondent over Fedwire/CHIPS and then spot-converted into CAD. The receiving bank files a FINTRAC Large EFT report for any transaction of CAD $10,000 or more. The treasury must reconcile each credit advice against the subscribed capital ledger and maintain the supporting board resolution to document that share issuance proceeds are credited to contributed surplus rather than taxable income.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Inbound digital-store receivables are collected as SWIFT MT103 USD wires from Valve (Steam monthly publisher settlement) and Sony (PlayStation Store partner settlement) into the CA_CORP USD operating account; the treasury then executes a spot USD/CAD FX conversion on the bank platform and funds CAD payroll, tax, and operational obligations via Lynx or internal electronic funds transfer. Outbound trade settlements to co-publishers, middleware licensors, royalty agents, and escrow depositaries are executed by SWIFT MT103 wires with the invoice/reference number quoted in the narrative; for high-value development-advance contracts, a Commercial Letter of Credit (import/export UC) may be opened or confirmed through the bank's trade-finance desk, with compliance with the UCP 600 rules. Every outbound cross-border wire of CAD $10,000 or more is reported to FINTRAC, and the FX conversion ticket must be retained for GST/HST audit support and for intercompany chargeback documentation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/CAD FX forward contracts (fixed-date and window/seasonal contracts) executed under the Canadian bank's ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and CSA, with tenors up to 24 months suited to Steam and PlayStation quarterly payout cycles
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in non-fully-convertible payout-market currencies (e.g., BRL, KRW, MXN, TRY) where local Steam/PlayStation regional sales produce residual currency translation risk
Cross-currency swaps (USD/CAD and USD/EUR) matching the currency profile of long-term platform royalty streams and co-publishing development advances
Vanilla European-style USD/CAD FX call and put options and zero-cost collars to cap downside conversion rates on USD remittances from Valve and Sony
Average-rate (Asian) window forward contracts enabling multiple monthly USD sweeps to be hedged at a blended quarterly rate
Foreign exchange swap (FX swap) transactions to cover temporary USD funding liquidity mismatches between Steam payout receipt dates and CAD disbursement obligations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ontario Annual Return (annual corporate declaration under the Ontario Business Corporations Act, OBCA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ontario Business Registry (OBR), Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, Province of Ontario
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days of the anniversary of incorporation, annually thereafter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of CAD 100 (approx. USD 74) in addition to the CAD 25 filing fee; failure to file for two consecutive years exposes the corporation to a 120-day notice of intent to dissolve and administrative dissolution under OBCA s. 240; delinquency also blocks issuance of compliance certificates for commercial closings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return (CBCA annual corporate return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED), Government of Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days of the anniversary of incorporation, annually thereafter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Filing fee of CAD 12 for online filing; two consecutive omitted annual returns generate a 60-day Notice of Default and risk of administrative dissolution under CBCA s. 212.1; unresolved delinquency prevents issuance of standing and compliance certificates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal corporate return also computes Ontario provincial corporate tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Corporate Income Tax Compliance Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before six months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., December 31 fiscal year-end due no later than June 30 next); quarterly installments are due for material balances
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty equal to 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per full month of delinquency up to 12 months; daily compound interest at the prescribed statutory rate applies on unpaid tax and installments; chronic non-filing permits CRA protected assessment and may trigger director liability for unremitted amounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Notice of Change of Directors/Officers (OBCA Form 2) — recurring corporate secretarial filing upon board seat changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ontario Business Registry (OBR), Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 calendar days of any director change (event-based, typically managed alongside each year's annual maintenance review)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Per-day late-filing penalties may apply under OBCA for omitted filings; inaccurate director records impair bank, Steam/Valve, and platform KYC verifications and can invalidate certificates of status.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent audit is mandatory for a distributing corporation (publicly traded securities). A non-distributing private Ontario/federal corporation may waive the auditor only where (i) gross annual revenues do not exceed CAD 1,000,000 and (ii) total assets do not exceed CAD 2,000,000 at the preceding fiscal year-end, and all shareholders consent (CBCA Reg. s. 82(2); OBCA O. Reg. 62/20). Audits are likewise required by shareholder requisition or by lender/investor agreements typical of publishing advances.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (Part I CPA Canada Handbook) for distributing corporations and any elective IFRS adopter; Canadian ASPE (Part II CPA Canada Handbook) for private non-distributing corporations; independent audits performed under Canadian Auditing Standards (CAS); T2 income tax reporting follows CRA-recognized GAAP with Part I statutory adjustments.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: OBCA Part IV.2 and CBCA s. 21.1 require a register of 'Individuals with Significant Control' (ISCs), i.e., individuals holding 25% or more of voting shares or carrying value, or exercising de facto control. The register must be updated and re-dated within 15 days of any share transfer producing an ISC change; no public annual filing of ISC details is presently due, but the annual return confirms whether ISCs exist and identifies the register location for inspection by the registrar or the CRA. Canada is phasing in a public beneficial ownership registry; once the enabling regulations are proclaimed, annual-return ISC declarations will populate that registry and on-site register production rights remain in force.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of directors' and shareholders' meetings and written consents
Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC Register)
Register of Share Transfers and share issuance transaction records
